text:
tess: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing we formalize a CP demarcation at the customer VPC edge instead of doing a single transit-gateway consolidation. sketching tradeoffs below, want quick takes before I turn this into an RFC revision.

kevin: curious — can you summarize the main operational differences?

maria: short high level: TGW consolidation = fewer peering objects, simpler billing model, but centralizes routing/egress and makes a bigger blast radius. per-edge demarc = more peering counts and routing tables to manage, but isolates customer faults and preserves srcIP semantics.

sam: +1 on srcIP preservation point. lots of customers rely on preserving source for firewall allowlists. if we NAT behind a central TGW we break that.

kevin: what's the limit hit for peering? AWS account/tgw limits might force us to shard anyway.

maria: right — there are soft limits: route table entries, peering attachments, and cross-account constraints. hitting >1000 tenants and tgws becomes messy. but we could use a small number of regional TGWs and bucket tenants by scale.

sam: ops question: how would cert/identity flow work if demarcation is at edge? do we terminate mTLS at our sidecar or at the customer endpoint?

kevin: demo idea: terminate mutual TLS at our relay sidecar inside the customer VPC (agent) so CP control plane certs never leave cust VPC. that keeps trust model tight but means we need a minimal agent footprint.

maria: that agent approach helps air-gapped customers too. downside: agent lifecycle and upgrade scars. we need a rollout plan: agentless fallback to central relay for onboarding.

tess: rollout plan I'm thinking: 1) new tenants default to edge-demarc with agent; 2) existing tenants opt-in via onboarding job; 3) central TGW remains fallback for <30d to catch edge failures. canary with small subset.

kevin: sounds safe. what about routing complexity? per-tenant route tables explode. can we use an L3 overlay (e.g., WireGuard mesh) to reduce AWS route pressure?

sam: overlay reduces route bloat but adds maintainability and throughput limits. also complicates traceroute and cost attribution.

maria: another option: consolidate egress at regional egress gateways but keep control-plane handoff at edge. so control plane auth happens at agent, but heavy egress (model traffic) can go via a regional relay optimized for throughput. middle ground.

kevin: agree — split control-plane demarcation and data-plane consolidation. control plane needs identity isolation; data plane prefers efficiency.

tess: good phrasing. two concrete operational must-haves: 1) stable customer-facing egress IP option (either preserve src IP or offer static NAT ranges customers can whitelist) and 2) automated routing table lifecycle (prune, backfill) to avoid entries leaking.

sam: for (1) we can offer: agent-preserve-srcip OR regional-static-nat (per-tenant elastic IP pool). choose per account.

maria: for (2) automation notes: incremental apply with idempotent tags, GC job that retires stale routes after TTL, and alert on route-table growth > threshold.

kevin: can we show a tiny terraform-ish snippet for the NAT option in the RFC appendix? something like:
```
resource "aws_eip" "tenant_nat" {
  count = var.tenant_requires_static_ip ? 1 : 0
}
resource "aws_nat_gateway" "tenant" {
  allocation_id = aws_eip.tenant_nat[0].id
  subnet_id = var.egress_subnet
}
```

tess: perfect — include that. one more edge case: cross-account routing when customers own the VPC vs when we provision. different consent/ops flows. need playbooks for both.

maria: playbook bullets: customer-owned VPC = provide onboarding manifest + agent image + TLS trust bundle. provider-owned VPC = we create peering/attachments and manage rotation but expose audit logs.

sam: monitoring: must have per-tenant control plane latency SLO, peering attach health, and NAT pool utilization dashboards. also route churn metrics.

infra-bot: new note: created ticket INFRA-9243 to track automation work (route GC, NAT pool allocator).

kevin: outstanding questions before we convert to RFC: cost model for regional egress vs central TGW, expected limit scaling and runbook for peering exhaustion.

tess: i'll add cost model sketch and a migration appendix with canary cutover steps + rollback plan. will post an RFC draft by EOD Friday. thanks for quick feedback :rocket:
